answer: An agent economy can make identity cost real: every participant locks a bond in a shared vault and receives one vote. Each epoch a random pulse selects a few voters to show a cedar seal of uniqueness; failure slashes their bond and ejects them. A sybil farmer must fund a full bond for each fake name and still faces the same audit odds per name, so expected loss grows linearly with clones while influence grows only one vote at a time. Impersonation costs more than honest work, and burned bonds pay the verifiers.
